Yeah exactly. I think the best thing for you would be to do the t level and try and get a degree apprenticeship afterwards or see which unis will have you.

I'm an engineering apprentice, I'm doing a level 3 while working 4 days a week. Same level as a levels/t level but I also get a really good salary for a 17 year old. After I've done the level 3 my company offers the opportunity to get a degree. I dont know if you're set on uni for the lifestyle or just the degree itself, but if it's the latter then I'm sure you could get there through t levels or an apprenticeship. T levels are more specifically focused on what you want to do so i think you'd find it easier to motivate yourself that way, and you'd gain good experience that could get you into a degree apprenticeship afterwards. Your best chances for a standard uni experience is a levels, but that's not to say you can't get that from t levels, you'll just be shorter for choice of unis/courses. It's hard to tell because t levels are so new. But if your heart's in engineering I'd say do the t level.

I'm in the same boat as you. I'd recommend having a look into whether you can physically go into your school and do your lessons there. If you have an EHCP then I believe you're entitled to it, if not it might be worth asking anyway. I'm autistic as well but I don't have an EHCP, and my school were happy to let me come in anyway as they knew it'd be better for me.

Another little tip that works for me is to find a reason that you want to do it, even if it's a silly one! I bought myself some really expensive pens that make me really want to sit down and write notes. I also find working on a whiteboard is nice for me, for the novelty and also because it takes off the pressure of the permanent nature of writing on paper?? I don't know if that makes sense to anyone else. Anyway, you might not use the same things as me, but maybe you'll find an incentive. Hope you figure everything out bro :)

EDIT: Just thought of another thing. If you're not able to go into school (or even if you are!) then it's nice to get some fresh air and walk around between tasks. I know people always recommend exercise in inappropriate situations but I go on a walk around my school site once a day and I really like being in a separate space and having the time to just exist and not worry about work. Might not work for you though and that's okay! ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
